title: Sicily Grand Circuit: Palermo, Etna & the Val di Noto
subRegion: Sicily — Palermo, Etna, the Ionian coast and the Val di Noto

bestPeriod.avoid: July–August (40°C inland, Taormina gridlock, hotel rates doubled); January–February for Etna road closures

accommodation.note: Palermo palazzo B&B, Ortigia boutique, one agriturismo

food.note: Street food in Palermo is €5; Ortigia seafood is €45

transport.note: Rental, fuel (~€1.85/l), A19/A20 tolls, ZTL-safe parking

activities.note: Valle dei Templi, Etna cable car, Segesta, Villa Romana

profile.difficultyNote: 2 — driving-led, with a 2 h optional crater walk on Etna and steep cobbled old towns

gatewayAirport: PMO — Palermo Falcone Borsellino; 35 km / 40 min to central Palermo on the A29. Return from CTA Catania is 30 min from Taormina
summary: Sicily is an island the size of Wales with the road inventory of a small country and the driving culture of a contact sport. This circuit runs anticlockwise from Palermo along the Tyrrhenian to Cefalù, climbs Etna's southern flank on the SP92, drops to Taormina and Siracusa, then works west through the Baroque hill towns of the Val di Noto to Agrigento's Greek temples before closing the loop at Segesta and Erice. The distances are modest — around 1,100 km — but almost none of it is fast: the autostrade are patchy and viaduct-limited, the provincial roads are beautiful and slow, and every historic centre is a Limited Traffic Zone with a camera on it. Suited to drivers who want density of sights over speed, and who will do the homework on ZTLs.

itinerary.title: Palermo without the car
itinerary.morning: Land at PMO and take the A29 into the city. Go directly to your hotel's arranged garage — do not attempt to find street parking inside the ring. Then leave the car alone for 24 hours.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk the Quattro Canti, the Cattedrale, and the Cappella Palatina in the Palazzo dei Normanni — the finest Arab-Norman mosaic room in Europe. Then the Ballarò or Capo market for panelle and sfincione.
itinerary.evening: Aperitivo on Piazza Sant'Anna, then dinner at Trattoria Ai Cascinari on Via d'Ossuna — order the sarde a beccafico and whatever pasta is on the blackboard.
itinerary.dayStats: 35 km / 40 min from PMO; A29 toll-free; garage €18–€25/night; ZTL active Mon–Fri 08:00–20:00.
itinerary.sleep: Palazzo Sitano or B&B Al Quattro Canti, Palermo — both arrange garage transfers.

itinerary.title: Monreale, the A20 and Cefalù
itinerary.morning: Drive 12 km up to Monreale for the cathedral's 6,000 m² of gold mosaic. Park in the Piazza Vittorio Emanuele paid lot; the approach is steep and narrow and coach-clogged after 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Back down and east on the A20 to Cefalù. Park at the Lungomare paid lots (blue lines, €1–€1.50/h) outside the centre — the old town is a seasonal ZTL. Climb the Rocca for the view over the tiled roofs, or settle for the cathedral's Christ Pantocrator.
itinerary.evening: Sunset from the old harbour beach with the cathedral behind you — the best light of the whole north coast. Dinner at Ristorante Kentia.
itinerary.dayStats: 95 km / 1 h 40; A20 toll ~€3.60 Palermo–Cefalù; Monreale parking €2/h; Rocca entry €5, 45 min climb.
itinerary.sleep: Hotel Kalura, Cefalù — outside the ZTL with its own free car park.

itinerary.title: Across the island to Etna's southern flank
itinerary.morning: Take the A19 south-east (toll-free) across the wheat interior, an underrated landscape of empty rolling gold. Detour to the Villa Romana del Casale at Piazza Armerina if you want the Roman mosaics — it adds 90 minutes.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb to Nicolosi, then the SP92 to Rifugio Sapienza at 1,910 m. The road threads black 2001 lava. From Sapienza, the cable car plus 4x4 bus reaches ~2,900 m; the cable car alone reaches 2,500 m and you walk the Silvestri craters for free at the car park.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Zafferana Etnea or Linguaglossa on the SP92/SP59 and eat at Ristorante Sabir in Zafferana — pasta alla Norma and Etna Rosso from Nerello Mascalese.
itinerary.dayStats: 210 km / 3 h 30 driving; SP92 climbs 1,200 m in 18 km, ~20 hairpins; Sapienza parking €4–€6; cable car + jeep €70–€95 pp; A19 toll-free.
itinerary.sleep: Shalai Resort, Linguaglossa — vineyard-side, secure parking, on the Etna Nord road.

itinerary.title: Taormina, where the car becomes a liability
itinerary.morning: Drive the SS120 and SS114 down to Taormina — 45 minutes. **Do not drive into Taormina.** Park at Parcheggio Lumbi or Porta Catania (€15–€25/day) and take the free shuttle up. The Corso and the whole upper town are closed to cars.
itinerary.afternoon: The Teatro Antico with Etna framed in the proscenium is the shot; go late afternoon when the coach tours have gone and the light is warm. Then the Villa Comunale gardens and a granita at Bam Bar.
itinerary.evening: Descend to Siracusa on the A18 (toll-free). Park in the Talete multi-storey at the top of Ortigia — the island is a ZTL and Talete is the legal entry. Dinner at Ristorante Regina Lucia on Piazza Duomo.
itinerary.dayStats: 145 km / 2 h 30; Taormina parking €15–€25 + free shuttle; Teatro Antico €14; Talete garage €1.50/h, ~€20/day; A18 toll-free.
itinerary.sleep: Algilà Ortigia Charme Hotel, Siracusa — arranges Talete parking and a ZTL permit for the drop-off.

itinerary.title: Ortigia dawn, then the Baroque hills
itinerary.morning: Walk Ortigia early: the Duomo built into a Greek temple, the Fonte Aretusa, and the Mercato di Ortigia which winds down by 13:00. Collect the car from Talete by 11:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Inland on the SS115 and SP to Noto, then Modica and Ragusa Ibla — three UNESCO Baroque towns in one afternoon. Park below Ragusa Ibla at the Piazza della Repubblica lots; Ibla itself is a ZTL of near-vertical alleys where a car is genuinely stuck. Modica's chocolate at Antica Dolceria Bonajuto is worth the queue.
itinerary.evening: Push west to Agrigento on the SS115 — a slow, truck-heavy road. Dinner at Ristorante Kalòs near the Valle dei Templi.
itinerary.dayStats: 240 km / 5 h with three town stops; SS115 averages 55 km/h; all ZTL — park outside every centre; fuel at Modica before the SS115 run.
itinerary.sleep: Villa Athena, Agrigento — the only hotel with the Temple of Concordia in its window; or Hotel Kaos for a third of the price.

itinerary.title: Valle dei Templi and the Scala dei Turchi question
itinerary.morning: Valle dei Templi at opening (08:30). Start at the Temple of Juno and walk down to Concordia — the best-preserved Doric temple outside Paestum. Two hours before the heat.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive 15 km to Realmonte for the Scala dei Turchi. **Access to the white marl staircase has been restricted since 2019** and sections remain closed on safety and erosion grounds; there is no free parking — use the private lots on the SP68. The reliable move is the viewpoint from Lido Rossello, 1 km east, which gives the whole cliff in profile without any access question.
itinerary.evening: North on the SS189/SS121 to Segesta country. Dinner and a bed at a Trapanese agriturismo; the Baglio Fontanasalsa area near Trapani does proper couscous alla trapanese.
itinerary.dayStats: 165 km / 3 h; Valle dei Templi €12, parking €5; Scala dei Turchi private parking €3–€5; SS115 and SS189 both single carriageway.
itinerary.sleep: Baglio Fontanasalsa, Trapani — restored olive estate, ample courtyard parking.

itinerary.title: Segesta, Erice and the drop-off
itinerary.morning: Segesta at opening: an unfinished 5th-century BC Doric temple standing alone in a field of fennel, and a theatre on the hill above reached by shuttle bus. This is the most atmospheric site on the island and the least crowded before 10:00.
itinerary.afternoon: Drive to Trapani and take the **funivia cable car** up to Erice rather than the SP31 hairpin road — the medieval town at 750 m is a ZTL, parking is scarce, and the cable car is €9.50 return and takes 10 minutes. Genovesi pastries at Maria Grammatico.
itinerary.evening: A29 back to PMO (45 min) and drop the car. If flying from CTA instead, allow 3 h 15 on the A19.
itinerary.dayStats: 105 km / 2 h to PMO; Segesta €6; Erice funivia €9.50 return; A29 toll-free; refuel before the airport spur.

accommodationStrategy.name: Palazzo Sitano
accommodationStrategy.description: Inside the historic centre but with a partnered garage on Via Roma and a driver who takes the car in for you, which removes the ZTL problem on arrival day entirely. Walking distance to Ballarò, the Cattedrale and the Vucciria. €110–€160 a double with breakfast on the terrace.

accommodationStrategy.name: Algilà Ortigia Charme Hotel
accommodationStrategy.description: The practical Ortigia choice: it issues a temporary ZTL permit for the drop-off and holds a discounted rate at the Talete garage, which is otherwise the difference between €20 a day and a €100 fine. Arab-Norman-styled rooms on a quiet lane a block from the Duomo. €150–€230.

accommodationStrategy.name: Shalai Resort
accommodationStrategy.description: On Etna's north flank, with private off-street parking and a Michelin-starred restaurant that saves you a post-volcano drive. Positioned for both the SP92 south approach and the Etna Nord road, and 45 minutes from Taormina without the coastal traffic. €160–€240.

logistics.connectivity: Italy is in the EU roaming zone. Coverage is good on the coast and thin in the Madonie and Iblei interiors. Download offline maps for the SP road network — many minor SP roads are mis-mapped or have been closed by landslip for years without the apps knowing.
logistics.emergency: 112 nationwide. 118 for medical, 115 for fire, 1530 for coastguard. Etna is monitored by INGV Osservatorio Etneo; the Guardia Forestale closes the summit access on activity. EHIC/GHIC covers state healthcare for eligible visitors.
logistics.weather: The **scirocco** brings Saharan dust and 40°C+ days to the south coast between May and September, sometimes coating the car in red silt. Etna generates its own weather — 30°C in Catania can be 8°C and blowing at Rifugio Sapienza. Ash fall closes CTA airport several times a year.
logistics.bookingWindows: Valle dei Templi and the Cappella Palatina benefit from online timed tickets in high season. The Etna cable car cannot be pre-booked and queues from 09:30. Taormina hotels sell out for the Taormina Film Fest in June. Aeolian ferries from Milazzo need 1–2 weeks' notice for vehicles, but see the rental note below.
logistics.money: Euro. Cards are near-universal now, including parking meters via app (EasyPark works island-wide). Keep €30 in coins for blue-line street parking. Coperto of €2–€3 per person is standard and is not a tip; tipping beyond rounding is not expected.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Italy. A20 is barrier-tolled — take a ticket, pay at the exit (cards accepted, avoid the yellow Telepass lanes). ZTL enforcement is camera-based and unforgiving; register your plate with your hotel where possible. Headlights are mandatory outside built-up areas. Alcohol limit 0.05%, and zero for drivers licensed under three years. **Taking a rental car on a ferry to the Aeolian Islands or the mainland requires written permission** — most companies refuse the Aeolians outright, so visit Salina or Lipari as a foot passenger from Milazzo and leave the car in the port lot.
logistics.permits: Etna's summit zone above 2,900 m may only be visited with an authorised alpine guide. Drones are banned over all archaeological sites and within 5 km of Catania and Palermo airports. Removing rock from Scala dei Turchi or lava from Etna carries substantial fines.
logistics.health: Tap water is potable but heavily chlorinated in Palermo and Agrigento; most locals drink bottled. Jellyfish (Pelagia noctiluca) blooms hit the Ionian coast in late summer. Etna's summit involves 3,000 m altitude — go slowly and bring a windproof layer regardless of the coastal temperature. Sun exposure at the archaeological sites is severe with no shade.

proTips: Treat every historic centre as undriveable and budget €15–€25 a day for garages. It is cheaper than one ZTL fine, and the fines arrive months later when you can no longer contest the signage.
In Taormina, park at **Lumbi**, not Porta Catania — Lumbi's free shuttle runs more often and drops you at Porta Messina, the correct end of the Corso for the Teatro Antico.
Photograph Segesta's temple in the first hour after opening, when the low sun rakes the columns and the fennel field is still in dew. By 11:00 it is flat, hot and full of coaches.

On Etna, skip the €90 jeep-to-summit package unless the weather is genuinely clear. The free Silvestri craters walk from the Rifugio Sapienza car park delivers 70% of the volcanic experience for nothing.
Refuel at "fai da te" (self-service) pumps and always before 19:30 inland. Attended service adds €0.20–€0.25 per litre, and rural stations close early and all day Sunday.

Buy the Valle dei Templi ticket that includes the Museo Archeologico Pietro Griffo — most people skip the museum, and it holds the giant Telamon that once stood in the Temple of Zeus you are looking at the ruins of.
Cefalù, Noto and Ragusa Ibla all look best in the hour before sunset when the local limestone goes gold. Structure the day around arriving in one of them at 18:00 rather than at lunchtime.

For Scala dei Turchi, go at sunrise or shoot it from Lido Rossello. Midday turns the white marl into a glare pit and the access situation is unpredictable enough that a guaranteed viewpoint beats a gamble.

Photograph the rental car's roof, wheels and underbody sills at pickup. Sicilian counters dispute roof and alloy damage more than anywhere else in Italy, and dashcam-quality photos with a timestamp are what wins the argument.

raw.Total distance: ~1,100 km over 7 days. Longest leg is Day 5, Siracusa–Agrigento via Modica and Ragusa, at 240 km but a genuine 5 h with the hill-town stops.
raw.SP92 Etna Sud (Nicolosi–Rifugio Sapienza: 18 km of climbing from ~700 m to 1,910 m, roughly 20 wide hairpins, excellent asphalt because it is rebuilt after every major eruption. It runs through 1983 and 2001 lava fields; the surface is grippy but the crosswinds above 1,500 m are real. Free to drive; the Rifugio Sapienza car park is €4–€6/day. Closes without notice during eruptive activity or snow — the Etna road can be shut into April.
raw.Autostrada tolls: the **A20 Messina–Palermo is tolled** (Messina–Palermo ~€11 for a car, collected at Villafranca, Barcellona, Tindari, Sant'Agata and Castelbuono barriers); the **A19 Palermo–Catania is toll-free**, as are the A18 Catania–Siracusa and the A29. Expect long viaduct sections of the A20 to be reduced to a single lane by permanent works.
raw.ZTL discipline — the single biggest cost: Palermo's ZTL covers the historic centre Mon–Fri roughly 08:00–20:00 with camera enforcement; Taormina's Corso Umberto is fully pedestrian with the whole upper town restricted; Siracusa's **Ortigia island is a ZTL with a resident-only core**; Cefalù, Ragusa Ibla, Modica and Noto all run seasonal ZTLs. Fines are €80–€120 per pass, arrive 6–12 months later via the rental company with a €40 admin fee, and each camera pass is a separate fine.
raw.Autovelox and tutor systems: fixed speed cameras are common on the SS113, SS114 and the A19, usually signed but sometimes only 150 m ahead. The A18 uses average-speed enforcement in sections. Rental fines are passed through automatically.
raw.Car rental & cross-border: Sicily is an island, so cross-border is a non-issue, but **ferry permission is not automatic** — taking a rental to the Aeolians or to the mainland usually requires written consent. One-way PMO-to-CTA drops are typically €40–€90; book the one-way explicitly at reservation, not at the counter. Sicilian rental desks are notorious for aggressive insurance upselling and for pre-existing damage disputes: photograph every panel and the roof before leaving.
raw.Fuel: widespread and rarely a problem, but many rural stations are **self-service only after 19:30** and some inland stations close entirely on Sunday. "Servito" pumps cost €0.20–€0.25/litre more than "fai da te". Expect ~€1.80–€1.95/litre for petrol.
raw.Driving hazards specific to Sicily: unsignalled roadworks with no taper; scooters filtering on both sides; livestock on the SP roads of the Madonie and the Iblei; and unlit single-bore tunnels on the SS624 and older SS113 sections. Right of way at roundabouts is treated as advisory.

sources.verified: Scala dei Turchi access status — the white cliffs remain partly restricted with sections off-limits since 2019, the site is privately owned, and there is no free parking (private lots on the SP68); the A20 Messina–Palermo is tolled while the A19 Palermo–Catania is toll-free; Sicilian ZTL enforcement practice and typical fine levels; Rifugio Sapienza at 1,910 m as the SP92 road head.
sources.confidenceNotes: Scala dei Turchi is the most volatile item in this file — access has been opened, restricted and re-restricted repeatedly and is subject to ongoing legal and erosion disputes; re-verify within days of publishing. Etna's SP92 and the cable car close without notice during eruptive episodes; INGV bulletins are the source of truth. ZTL hours and boundaries in Cefalù, Noto and Ragusa are set municipally and change seasonally — always confirm against the comune's own site rather than a travel blog. A20 toll totals and Etna cable car prices are revised annually. Rental one-way drop charges and ferry-permission policies vary by company and should be confirmed in the booking terms, not at the desk.
